analysis.title: Cisco Systems Inc. (CSCO) F1Q27 First Take: Beat on raise on Networking revenue; strong margin outlook
key_insights: CSCO F1Q27 non-GAAP EPS of $1.40 beat GS/consensus of $1.33/$1.32 and company guidance of $1.32-$1.34. GS's bottom line is that the stock should trade higher on the beat and raise.
F1Q27 revenue of $18.5bn (+24% yoy) beat GS/consensus of $18.1bn/$18.1bn and guidance of $18.0-$18.2bn. The beat was primarily driven by Networking.

Networking revenue of $11.1bn (+43% yoy) beat GSe/consensus of $10.7bn/$10.7bn. Security ($2.1bn, +7% yoy) and Collaboration ($1.1bn, +8% yoy) were in line. Observability ($279mn, +2% yoy) missed GSe/consensus of $282/$285mn.

Non-GAAP gross margin of 65.6% was slightly below GSe of 66.0% but in line with consensus of 65.6% and at the midpoint of the 65%-66% guidance. Non-GAAP EBIT margin of 37.8% beat GS/consensus of 36.8%/36.2% and the 35.5%-36.5% guidance midpoint, which GS reads as strong operating leverage.
Non-GAAP EBIT of $7.0bn beat GSe/consensus of $6.7bn/$6.5bn. Operating expenses of $5,140mn were below GS's $5,287mn estimate.
Buybacks of $2.0bn beat GS's $1.25bn estimate and rose from $1.5bn in the prior quarter.

F2Q27 guidance is above consensus: revenue $18.0-$18.2bn (consensus $17.8bn), non-GAAP gross margin 65-66% (consensus 64.4%), non-GAAP EBIT margin 36-37% (consensus 34.7%), non-GAAP EPS $1.34-$1.36 (consensus $1.23). GAAP EPS guide is $1.07-$1.09.

FY2027 guidance was raised: revenue $74.8-$75.8bn (prior $72.2-$73.4bn, consensus $72.9bn) and non-GAAP EPS $5.47-$5.53 (prior $5.05-$5.11, consensus $5.10). GAAP EPS guide is $4.38-$4.44 (prior $4.00-$4.06). The GAAP tax rate is now about 16% (prior about 14.5%) and the non-GAAP tax rate is unchanged at about 18.5%.

GS keeps a Neutral rating and a $125 12-month target price (25x NTM+1Y EPS), 24.1% above the $100.76 price. The thesis is that Cisco is the networking market-share leader with wide product breadth, but has lost share over the past decade to lower-cost and specialist competitors such as white box, ANET and FFIV.

Backlog, RPO and ARR give revenue visibility even if order growth slows. GS's risks include Huawei and H3C, white-box competition, margin pressure from a mix shift toward cloud customers, supply chain costs, hardware commoditization and dilutive acquisitions.

market_movers.rationale: GS stays Neutral with a $125 target (25x NTM+1Y EPS), 24.1% above the $100.76 price, after a beat and raise on Networking revenue. The report says the stock should trade higher on the print.

earnings_insights: CSCO F1Q27 (reported 11/12/2026): non-GAAP diluted EPS $1.40 reported vs GSe $1.33 and consensus $1.32 (+39% yoy from $1.00). GAAP EPS was $1.14 vs GS's $1.03 (+60% yoy).
F1Q27 revenue $18,517mn reported (+24% yoy) vs GSe $18,120mn and consensus $18,071mn. Product revenue was $14,667mn (+32%) and services $3,850mn (+1%).
F1Q27 non-GAAP operating income $7,007mn reported vs GSe $6,669mn and consensus $6,541mn. Margin was 37.8% vs GSe 36.8% and consensus 36.2%, up 3.4pp yoy.
Non-GAAP gross margin was 65.6% reported, down 2.5pp yoy from 68.1%, vs GSe 66.0% and consensus 65.6%. Cost of sales rose 34% yoy against 24% revenue growth.

F2Q27 guidance (company): revenue $18.0-$18.2bn vs consensus $17.8bn, non-GAAP EPS $1.34-$1.36 vs consensus $1.23. Gross margin 65-66% vs consensus 64.4%. EBIT margin 36-37% vs consensus 34.7%. Non-GAAP tax rate about 18.5% and GAAP tax rate about 14.5%.
FY2027 guidance (company, raised): revenue $74.8-$75.8bn vs prior $72.2-$73.4bn and consensus $72.9bn. Non-GAAP EPS $5.47-$5.53 vs prior $5.05-$5.11 and consensus $5.10.

GS's own FY7/27E estimates are revenue $72,686mn and EPS $5.06 (est, diluted, pre-exceptionals), both below the raised guidance ranges. GS's F2Q27E EPS is $1.33 (10/26E column), below the $1.34-$1.36 guide. This implies upward estimate revisions, though the report does not state the new figures.
risk_factors: Competition, including from Huawei and H3C and from white-box solutions.
Margin degradation from a mix shift to more cloud customers and elevated supply chain costs.
Broader pricing pressure from commoditization of networking hardware.
Order growth could slow in the near term as customers absorb previously placed orders and scrutinize IT budgets in a challenging macro environment.
